newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends off on mixed selling, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends off on mixed selling, trade thin.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended a dull session weaker as activity calmed and prices consolidated gains from recent sessions, market sources said.

"We've been up for five days and it's not unusual to come down a bit," said Ernest Simon, a vice president with Prudential Securities. "We'll come down further once we begin to focus on the demand side."
He put support basis the December contract in the low 70.00-cent a lb range.
Prices got a boost on the open from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's export sales report, which pegged sales for the week ended Sept 19 at 131,700 bales.

But imports for the week ended Sept 22 totaled 36,377 bales, more than last week's exports of 33,300 bales. Trade and local selling and some profit-taking by the funds, pressured the market, but scale-down speculative and commission house buying supported prices at the lows.
The most-active December contract settled at 76.84, off 0.37, having ranged from 77.40 to 76.40. The back other months closed 0.50 to 0.32 lower.
